world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.note: Only Smythe/Z'graggen comparative wordlists, Blust fieldnotes, and vernacular story booklets; no phonology or grammar of Nali

new_statements.quote: The languages of the Admiralty Islands may be resolved into three major groups on the basis of their phonetic features listed in Table 1. [...] TABLE 1. PRINCIPAL PHONETIC DISTINGUISHING FEATURES OF ADMIRALTY ISLANDS LANGUAGES: Group 1 | Group 2 | Group 3 [...] main position of accent: penultimate | initial | final; rhythm: stress-timed | syllable-timed | mixed type; tones: - | - | + in some dialects [...] Group 3: Languages having complex phonetic systems, and closed syllables extremely common [...] Family 4. c. Rossun, Lauis, Yiru, Kapor, Sirra, Sonilu, Bulihan, Katin, Bua (Pwa), Malei
new_statements.citation: Smythe, W.E. (ed. Alan Healey). 1970. Melanesian, Micronesian, and Indonesian features in languages of the Admiralty Islands. In S.A. Wurm & D.C. Laycock (eds.), Pacific linguistic studies in honour of Arthur Capell, 1209-1234. Pacific Linguistics C-13. Canberra: Australian National University.
new_statements.locator: p.1209 sec. 1 (framing sentence) and Table 1, p.1211, rows 'main position of accent' and 'rhythm', column 'Group 3'; Yiru (= Nali) classified as Group 3 language 3A4c in Table 2 p.1212 and Family 4c list p.1213
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Files checked in (the target record's 'held' list is empty but the folder exists with the other reader's; I appended a dated independent-check note to it). (1) QUOTE: 26 pp., sealang CC BY-SA scan with text layer) -- p.1209 sec.1 reads verbatim 'The languages of the Admiralty Islands may be resolved into three major groups on the basis of their phonetic features listed in Table 1.'; the page render and text layer line 265) shows TABLE 1 'PRINCIPAL PHONETIC DISTINGUISHING FEATURES OF ADMIRALTY ISLANDS LANGUAGES' with rows 'main position of accent: penultimate | initial | final', 'rhythm: stress-timed | syllable-timed | mixed type', 'tones: - | - | + in some dialects' for Groups 1|2|3 exactly…
new_statements.rule_in_words: For the Manus group of Admiralty languages (Smythe's Group 3, which includes Yiru = Nali as language 3A4c), the main position of word accent is the final syllable, with 'mixed' (neither clearly stress- nor syllable-timed) rhythm. This is a group-level generalization across some two dozen Manus languages, not a Nali-specific description.
new_statements.exceptions: None for accent in Table 1 (other rows carry per-language exceptions such as 'except in Ponam', 'except in Sisi', showing the table is meant to hold group-wide unless flagged). The paper's only language-specific stress note (n.13, p.1232) concerns Gele' (Kele): phonemic stress tending to long vowels, penult of reduplications, and otherwise final syllables. Blust's 1975 Nali field transcriptions (RB2-011 pp.20-33, on file) show final stress ticks on most numerals but initial/penultimate ticks on several disyllabic nouns, so the Nali facts may be less uniform than 'final'.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level 'main position of accent' in a typological feature table compiled by a fieldworker who collected wordlists for all Admiralty languages (1940s-50s); no definition of domain, no examples for Nali. The Nali-specific SIL Organised Phonology Data (2 pp., archive 42320, 2011) would supersede this but could not be fetched sources.
new_statements.identity_note: Smythe 1970 refers to Nali as 'Yiru' (language 3A4c; villages Rossun, Lauis, Yiru, Kapor, Sirra, Sonilu, Bulihan, Katin, Bua, Malei = the Nali area of SE Manus, glottocode nali1245), but his accent statement is made for his whole Group 3 (all Manus and adjacent-island languages), not for Yiru individually. Blust's 1975 notebook data are from Lahan village (speaker Pokanas Popat), also Nali proper. The unfetched SIL OPD is catalogued under Nali [nss].

sources.note: Table 1 p.1211 'Principal phonetic distinguishing features', row 'main position of accent': Group 1 (Aua, Wuvulu) penultimate, Group 2 (Seimat, Kaniet) initial, Group 3 (Manus and adjacent islands) final; 'rhythm': mixed type for Group 3; Yiru (=Nali) is Group 3 language 3A4c (Table 2 p.1212, Family 4c p.1213). Group-level generalization only; no Nali-specific sentence.
